evidence: src/csv.js renderField (lines ~6-13): the wrapping branch returns `"${text}"` with no .replace/replaceAll doubling of embedded double quotes, only the regex test /[",\n\r]/
grep -rn "replace" src/ found only src/rows.js:9 (thousands-grouping .replace) — no quote-escape call anywhere in src/

node run: toCsv([{name:'A',key:'a'}], [{a:'He said "hi"'}]) produced "A\n\"He said \"hi\"\"" i.e. `A\n"He said "hi""` — field is quoted but the embedded `"` is not doubled, contradicting README rule and the test expecting `"He said ""hi"""`

README (authoritative spec) assigns the doubling rule to toCsv itself: under 'CSV rules' it says 'Inside a quoted field, every double quote is escaped by doubling (`""`)' and 'A quote inside a field that is not itself doubled produces malformed CSV', and the Public API lists src/csv.js: toCsv as the writer that must not change — nothing assigns escaping to the shaping layer.
test/csv.test.js:15-18 calls toCsv directly with raw unescaped input ({ a: 'He said "hi"' }) and expects 'A,B\n"He said ""hi""",y', proving toCsv itself is required to double quotes.

Running npm test shows the failure is in toCsv's renderField: actual 'A,B\n"He said "hi"",y' vs expected 'A,B\n"He said ""hi""",y' (test/csv.test.js:16), and the identical malformed output in export.test.js:18 — src/csv.js:7-9 wraps the field in quotes but never doubles internal quotes.

Instrumenting shapeOrderRow: node output {"sku":"A-1","title":"He said \"hi\"","amount":"12,345.67","date":"2026-08-28"} — title keeps a single un-doubled quote, but export.test.js explicitly comments 'rows.js is correct per spec; the CSV writer must survive both', so this pass-through is per spec.

grep shows the only .replace in src/ is src/rows.js:9 (formatAmount digit grouping); there is no quote pre-escaping anywhere — but that is not a missing step, since the spec mandates doubling inside toCsv.

args.summary:
Root cause: In src/csv.js, renderField decided whether to wrap a field with quotes using the regex /[",\n\r]/, but when wrapping it interpolated the raw text without doubling embedded double quotes. So a field like `He said "hi"` was emitted as `"He said "hi""` (malformed CSV), contradicting the README rule that "Inside a quoted field, every double quote is escaped by doubling (`""`)."

Fix: In the wrapping branch of renderField, escape embedded double quotes by doubling them before interpolation: `return \`"${text.replaceAll('"', '""')}"\``. No other files changed; exported names and dependencies untouched.

Verified: `node --test --test-isolation=none` passes all 12 tests (csv quoting/doubling, export, format, dates, row shaping). Plain `node --test` cannot run in this sandbox due to spawn EPERM from child-process isolation, per the environment note.
